feedback: PASS with warnings. TDD is well-structured, traceable, technically accurate (README.md verified). OQ-1 (+1 vs +2 line delta) must be resolved in favor of +1 (ADR-002 Option 2, no blank separator) to satisfy PRD AT-1's strict 'exactly one greater' wording. T-6 hex-dump check and 54/135 byte counts are over-engineered for a trivial docs change; recommend replacing T-6 with a behavioral 'file ends with newline' check. No blocking findings; downstream plan/spec phases should adopt these resolutions.

findings.message: ADR-002 reinterprets PRD AT-1 ('exactly one greater') to permit a +2 line delta. Resolve OQ-1 in favor of Option 2 (no blank separator) so AT-1 is satisfied as written; the TDD already provides this fallback.

T-6 (`tail -c 1 README.md | xxd` checking for byte 0a) is a brittle hex-dump postcondition on a trivial docs change. Replace with a behavioral check such as `[ -z "$(tail -c1 README.md | tr -d '\n')" ]` or rely on FR-6 verification via diff/grep.
The 'Approximate size pre-change: 54 bytes / Post-change: ~135 bytes' contract is manufactured rigor for a docs-only edit; either drop it or label clearly as non-binding.
OQ-1 is left open in the TDD; this review resolves it (use +1 interpretation, Option 2). Plan/spec phases should treat ADR-002 as superseded accordingly.
